steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been going since you finished the program with us? Are you still keeping the weight off and feeling great, has a little started to creep back, or are you pretty much back to where you were before you started?

(This question has only three possible answers. Click the one you hear.)

steps.title: Doing Well on Program: Celebrate the Win
steps.content:
That’s wonderful to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That’s exactly what we like to hear, and you should be proud of the progress you’ve made.

Do you remember where you started? How you felt before the weight started coming off? (Let them enjoy the moment. This is their win.)

(Do not pitch anything yet. The file update comes next, and the close follows if nothing else surfaces.)

steps.title: Weight Creeping Back: No Blame, Then Update the File
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I really appreciate you telling me that, and I want you to hear something important: what you’re describing is not a failure, and it’s not a lack of willpower. It’s simply how these medications work. They quiet the appetite signals while you’re on them, and when the medication stops, those signals come back. That’s pharmacology, not character.

(Let them respond. Many people carry real shame about this. Take it off their shoulders before you go anywhere else.)

(Do not pitch anything yet. The file update comes next, and the close follows if nothing else surfaces.)

steps.title: Weight Fully Back: Warmest Version, Then Update the File
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, thank you for being honest with me, and please hear this first: you did not fail. The weight coming back after stopping these medications is the most common outcome there is. The medication was doing a real job, and when it stopped, the appetite signals it was quieting came back. That’s how they work, nobody tells people that clearly enough.

(Let them respond fully. This person likely feels defeated. Your whole job in this moment is warmth, zero judgment.)

And here’s what I want you to know: everything you did before still counts. You know the program, and you know how your body responds.

(Do not pitch anything yet. The file update comes next, and the close follows if nothing else surfaces.)

steps.title: Booked: Wrap Up Warm
steps.content:
Perfect, you’re all set for (day) at (time), {{contact_first_name}}.

We’ll take a fresh look at everything when you’re in. Where things stand today, and the right plan from here. All you have to do is show up.

We can’t wait to see you!

steps.title: The Transition: Update the File
steps.content:
Now {{contact_first_name}}, while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few quick questions so we get your file completely up to date. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes before starting the questions.)

steps.title: The Transition: Update the File
steps.content:
Now {{contact_first_name}}, while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few quick questions so we get your file completely up to date. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes before starting the questions.)

steps.title: The Six Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Ask these in order. Critical: write down everything they mention. You’ll read it back before the recommendation. Never give medical advice or discuss medication specifics on the call.)

Now, you mentioned the weight is staying off. That’s fantastic. One thing I’ll ask: how’s your energy and appetite been? Steady and comfortable, or anything that’s felt off lately?

Are the eating habits you built during the program still mostly in place? The protein, the portions, or has life pulled you back toward some of the old patterns?

How’s your strength and muscle tone been feeling? Keeping up with any activity, or has that been harder to hold onto?

How have you been sleeping? Falling asleep okay, staying asleep, waking up rested?

Beyond the weight itself, is there anything else health-wise that’s been on your mind? Energy dips, joints, stress. Anything you’ve been meaning to ask a professional about?

Last one, and it’s my favorite. If you could wave a wand and change just one thing about how you feel day to day, no judgment, what would it be?

(If they mentioned anything at all, read it back and click the first button. If truly nothing surfaced, fall through to the check-in close. That’s still a great call.)

steps.title: The Six Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Ask these in order. Critical: write down everything they mention. You’ll read it back before the recommendation. Never give medical advice or discuss medication specifics on the call.)

You mentioned some of it’s come back. Can I ask about how much we’re talking, and when you started noticing it? Was it right after stopping, or more gradual?

Are the eating habits from the program still mostly in place, or did the appetite coming back pull things toward the old patterns? (No judgment. That’s the medication wearing off, not willpower.)

How’s your energy been through all of it? Steady, or more ups and downs than before?

How have you been sleeping? Falling asleep okay, staying asleep, waking up rested?

Beyond the weight itself, is there anything else health-wise that’s been on your mind? Joints, stress, anything you’ve been meaning to ask a professional about?

Last one, and it’s my favorite. If you could wave a wand and change just one thing about how you feel day to day, no judgment, what would it be?

(If they mentioned anything beyond getting back on the program, read it back and click the first button. If getting back on track is the whole story, fall through to the close.)

steps.title: The Review & Bridge to Emotion
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I've got this right. (Recap what they told you: how long it's been going on, how often, and how it's been affecting them.) Did I get that right?

And it sounds like what you'd really love is to get back to feeling the way you did when things were going well. Is that fair to say?

(About 95% say yes. That yes is the moment. Don't rush past it.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, what I’d like to do now is ask you a few quick questions about {{main_concern}}, so I can get your file fully updated. It’ll only take a minute.

(Take the concern they named and make it real with three questions, in order. Write down or make note of their answers. You will use them in the next section. After each question, pause and let them fully answer. React like a human: “I see,” “Wow,” “That’s a lot.”)

How long has that been going on? A few weeks, a couple months, since things changed with the medication, or longer than that?

(Let them answer, then:) “[Repeat their answer back]? Would you agree with me that dealing with something like that for that long really isn’t OK?”

(If they shrug it off, “oh, I just deal with it”:) “You took a big step when you started this journey. You shouldn’t have to just put up with this part of it.”

And is it something you notice once in a while, or is it there pretty much every day at this point?

(Let them answer, then:) “That’s a lot. And honestly, carrying that around every day isn’t just not OK. It’s not something you have to live with. Wouldn’t you agree?”

And the last thing I’d like to ask is how it’s impacting you. But first, do me a favor: think of a day when you felt great. Energy up, feeling in control, everything clicking. Now think of the day it’s felt the worst. Do you have those two days in your head?

(Wait for the yes. Then walk that worst day through three areas, pausing after each:)

“On that day, what about work? Were you as productive as usual, as enjoyable to be around?” (Let them respond. “I see.”)

“What about at home? Were you fully engaged with the people around you, or did you kind of want to be left alone?” (Let them respond. “That’s really not OK.”)

“And the things you enjoy. Your hobbies, getting together with friends, family things. What happens to those on days like that?” (Let them open up. Do not rush.)

Then respond with empathy: Thank you for sharing that with me. It makes complete sense, and that’s exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}} help people with every single day.

steps.title: They Hesitate: Uncover Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you did mention {{main_concern}} is something you'd like to feel better about. I don't want to assume anything. Is the timing just not right, or is there something else on your mind that's holding you back from taking a look?

(Warm and easygoing, no pressure, and never restate the concern back at them. You're just trying to understand what's in the way. Then stop and let them answer.)

What are your thoughts about that?

steps.title: The Magic Question & Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, based on what you’ve shared with me, it sounds to me like {{main_concern}} isn’t just affecting you. It may also be affecting the people you care about, keeping you from the things you enjoy doing, maybe even getting in the way at work. Do you see how that could actually be the case?

(Wait for their answer. If they say no or hesitate:) “That’s completely fair, maybe it hasn’t reached that point yet. But it’s still been bothering you, and that’s reason enough.”

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you set up with an appointment so {{rec_pronoun}} can take a look at where things are and help you with {{main_concern}}. And I’ll tell you the same thing I tell everyone: if {{rec_pronoun}} think there’s something {{rec_pronoun}} can do to help you, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll let you know, and {{rec_pronoun}}’d be honored if you let {{rec_obj}}. And if for some reason {{rec_pronoun}} don’t think it’s the right fit, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll tell you that too, because the last thing {{rec_pronoun}} want to do is waste your time or your money. Does that sound reasonable?

(Ask “does that sound reasonable”, never “does that sound good.” Click what you hear next.)

steps.title: Nothing Surfaced: The Check-In Close
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I’m really glad everything’s going so well. That’s exactly what we like to hear.

Now, there is one thing I want to mention before I let you go. With these medications, the results you keep are all about staying dialed in. The dosing, how you’re tolerating it, protecting your muscle while the weight comes off. And your body today isn’t the same body we calibrated for months ago. What was tuned exactly right then can quietly drift out of tune as the weight comes off. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes. If they hesitate, use the button below to uncover the real concern.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation? (Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is we get you in for a quick check-in. That way we make sure your dosing and everything else is tuned exactly right for where your body is today. Does that sound reasonable?

(Wait for the yes.)

Okay, let’s get you on the schedule. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Getting Back On Track Is the Story: The Close
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, thank you for that. Your file is completely up to date.

And here’s the good news: the door is wide open, nothing about where you are today keeps you from getting back on track, and under proper supervision the restart is straightforward. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation? (Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is we get you back on the program now, picking up right where you left off, with the dosing managed correctly from day one. That’s the fastest path to feeling in control again. Does that sound reasonable?

(Wait for the yes.)

Okay, let’s get you back on the schedule. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: I gained it back as soon as I stopped
steps.content:
I completely understand, and that can happen from time to time, because the appetite tends to come right back when you stop. That's exactly why coming in makes sense, so {{rec_pronoun}} can look at the whole picture and talk through the best plan to get you back on track and keep it off.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I’m embarrassed I gained it back
steps.content:
Please don't be. The appetite signals the medication was quieting come back when it stops. That's how these medications work. It's pharmacology, not willpower, and it's exactly why we reach out, with no judgment at all. {{rec_pronoun_cap}}'d simply love to help you get back to where you were.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: Side effects or a bad experience before
steps.content:
(Acknowledge it warmly. Never give medical advice or discuss medication specifics on the call.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I completely understand, and I'm glad you told me. That's exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}}'ll want to talk through with you in person, so you can look at the whole picture together.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I need to think about it
steps.content:
That's completely fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's the right fit, which one is closest for you?

(Listen, their answer usually points to one of the other buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

Honestly, coming in is really just information. We take a look at where you're at with {{main_concern}}, you find out exactly what your options are, and then you get to decide with real answers instead of wondering. And if it's not the right fit, we'll tell you that too.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: Just send me information
steps.content:
I'd be glad to get you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a link or a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't look at where you're actually at and what would work best for you. That's really what the visit is for: we take a look and you get answers that apply to you, not just general information. So let me get you on the schedule first, and you'll have real answers to go on.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?
